observations: Retail packaging for a Krisdonia brand power bank.
The box identifies the product as a 'PD/DC Laptop Power Bank'.
The image on the box shows a device with a digital display (showing 100% 20V), two DC-OUT ports, a PD-100W port, and two USB-A ports.
The brand name 'Krisdonia' is printed in gold lettering on the box.
A watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI ARAMIDE KAFAYAT' is overlaid on the image.
The actual power bank is not visible; only the cardboard box is shown.
The box appears to be sitting on a dark wooden surface.

claims.evidence: The specific capacity (e.g., mAh or Wh) is not visible on the front of the box or the device.
The box art shows DC and PD ports; no AC outlet is visible on the pictured device.

risks.risk: The box may be empty or contain a different, inferior item.
risks.proof: A photo of the actual device outside of the packaging.

risks.risk: The battery capacity (mAh) is unknown, which significantly affects value.
risks.proof: A photo of the technical specifications label on the back of the box or the device itself.
risks.if_unproven: at the lowest capacity model in this range

risks.risk: The device may be faulty or unable to hold a charge.
risks.proof: A video showing the device powering on and successfully charging a laptop.

proof_requests: Photo of the actual power bank outside the box.
Photo of the specifications label (usually on the back or bottom) showing the mAh/Wh capacity.
Video of the device charging a laptop to verify the PD/DC output functionality.
response.reason: Only the retail box is shown. Without seeing the actual device and its specific capacity (mAh), it is impossible to verify the item's existence, condition, or correct market value.
